title: Cohomology of a finite base change of the ground field, with Frobenius the r-th power
statement: Let $k_0$ be a finite field, $\ell$ a prime different from the characteristic of $k_0$, and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ an algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ (Lean `PadicAlgCl ℓ`). Weil complexes on a $k_0$-scheme $X$ are the objects of the category $\mathrm{WC}(X)$ of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] (Lean `WeilComplex k₀ ℓ X`). Let $X$ be a $k_0$-scheme, quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of finite type over $k_0$, let $k_0'/k_0$ be an extension of finite fields of degree $r=[k_0':k_0]$, and let $i\in\mathbf Z$. Write $H^i(X)=H^i(X\otimes_{k_0}\bar k,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ for the cohomology of the constant Weil sheaf ([def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]) with its geometric Frobenius $F$ ([def-weil-frobenius-detailed]), and $H^i(X')$ with geometric Frobenius $F'$ of $k_0'$ for the base change $X'=X\times_{k_0}k_0'$ as a $k_0'$-scheme. Then there is a $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-linear isomorphism $e\colon H^i(X')\to H^i(X)$ with $e\circ F'=F^r\circ e$.

proof.text: Put $Y=X\times_{k_0}k_0\prime$, $q=\#k_0$ and $q\prime=\#k_0\prime$. Since $k_0\prime$ is a finite set, choose a maximal linearly independent list over $k_0$; it spans, since otherwise one could append another vector. Its length is $r=[k_0\prime:k_0]$. Taking coordinates gives a bijection $k_0\prime\simeq k_0^r$, so $q\prime=q^r$ and $r\ge1$ because $1\ne0$. This is the elementary basis-counting argument, not a separate lemma obligation (also Mathlib Module.card_eq_pow_finrank). The finite-field power identity gives $z^{q\prime}=z$ for every $z\in k_0\prime$. Thus each $z$ is a root of the nonzero polynomial $T^{q\prime}-T\in k_0[T]$ ($q\prime\ge2$), proving $k_0\prime/k_0$ algebraic. The field homomorphism $k_0\to k_0\prime$ is injective, so the two characteristics coincide.

proof.text: Let $\Omega$ and $\Omega\prime$ be the algebraic closures used to form the geometric fibers over $k_0$ and $k_0\prime$. Apply [lem-pod-algebraic-extension-closure-equivalence] to the algebraic extension established in step 1, obtaining a $k_0$-isomorphism $a:\Omega\prime\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega$. No equality of the independently chosen closures is assumed. Denote their structure maps by $j:k_0\to\Omega$ and $j\prime:k_0\prime\to\Omega\prime$.

Write $\overline Y=(X\times_{k_0}k_0\prime)\times_{k_0\prime}\Omega\prime$ and $\overline X=X\times_{k_0}\Omega$. Construct $u:\overline Y\to\overline X$ by its two projections: the composite to $X$, and $\operatorname{Spec}(a^{-1})$ after the projection to $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\prime$. They agree over $k_0$ because $a$ is a $k_0$-map. Conversely, the projection $\overline X\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ followed by $\operatorname{Spec}(a)$ gives its map to $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\prime$, hence to $\operatorname{Spec}k_0\prime$ via $\operatorname{Spec}(j\prime)$. Together with the projection to $X$ these maps first give a map to $Y$ and then to $\overline Y$. On composing in either order the projections to $X$ and the respective closure spectra are unchanged; uniqueness in the fiber-product universal property proves that these maps are inverse. Thus $u$ is an isomorphism of schemes.

proof.text: Let $\phi(z)=z^q$ on $\Omega$ and $\phi\prime(z)=z^{q\prime}$ on $\Omega\prime$ be arithmetic Frobenius, and put $\gamma=\phi^{-1}$, $\gamma\prime=(\phi\prime)^{-1}$. Induction gives $\phi^r(z)=z^{q^r}$; since $a$ preserves powers and $q\prime=q^r$, one has $a\phi\prime=\phi^r a$. Taking inverses gives $a\gamma\prime=\gamma^r a$, equivalently $\gamma\prime a^{-1}=a^{-1}\gamma^r$. The scheme automorphisms $\tau_Y,\tau_X$ are identity on the model and induced by these geometric field Frobenii on the closure factor. The maps $u\tau_Y$ and $\tau_X^r u$ have the same projection to $X$. Their projections to $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ agree by the last field identity and contravariance of Spec. The universal property of $\overline X$ therefore gives $u\tau_Y=\tau_X^r u$. This calculation compares geometric Galois Frobenius, not the absolute scheme Frobenius.

proof.text: The structure map of $X$ is of finite type because it is locally of finite type and quasi-compact. By [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], the structure map of $Y$ over $k_0\prime$ is of finite type, in particular locally of finite type and quasi-compact. By clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] it is quasi-separated. Also $\ell$ is invertible in both finite fields, since their characteristics agree by step 1. These are exactly the hypotheses for the geometric-cohomology comparison; no separatedness, smoothness, properness or geometric connectedness is required.

proof.text: Apply [def-pod-cohomology-geometric-equivalence] to $X/k_0$, $Y/k_0\prime$ and $u:\overline Y\simeq\overline X$. It supplies a $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-linear equivalence $e_i:H^i(\overline Y,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)\simeq H^i(\overline X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ for every $i\in\mathbf Z$, using precisely constant-Weil-sheaf cohomology. By [lem-pod-cohomology-geometric-conjugacy], the equation $u\tau_Y=\tau_X^r u$ from step 4 implies $e_i(F\prime x)=F^r e_i(x)$ for every $x$. For the specified $i$, take $e=e_i$. This proves the requested existence and intertwining equation on the same linear equivalence.

theorem exists_linearEquiv_cohomology_baseChangeField
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] [QuasiSeparated (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    (k₀' : Type u) [Field k₀'] [Finite k₀'] [Algebra k₀ k₀'] (i : ℤ) :
    haveI := fact_ringChar_ne_of_algebra (l := l) k₀ k₀'
    ∃ e : ((adicConstant k₀' l (X.baseChangeField k₀ k₀')).cohomology i).carrier ≃ₗ[PadicAlgCl l]
        ((adicConstant k₀ l X).cohomology i).carrier,
      ∀ x, e (((adicConstant k₀' l (X.baseChangeField k₀ k₀')).cohomology i).frobenius x) =
        (((adicConstant k₀ l X).cohomology i).frobeniusEnd ^ Module.finrank k₀ k₀') (e x) :=
  sorry
